newsitem.title: FINLAND: U.S., Russia agree on targets for WTO, Paris Club.
newsitem.headline: U.S., Russia agree on targets for WTO, Paris Club.

text.p: The United States and Russia agreed on Friday to set 1997 as a target for Russia to join the Paris Club and 1998 for Russian membership of the World Trade Organisation (WTO).

"The presidents set as a target that both sides would undertake best efforts for Russia, on commercial conditions generally applicable to newly acceding members, to join the World Trade Organisation in 1998, and to join the Paris Club in 1997 assuming agreement on conditions of membership," a joint U.S.-Russian statement said after a summit in Helsinki.
"Presidents Clinton and Yeltsin affirmed that cooperation to integrate Russia's economy into the global economic system represents one of their most important priorities," they said.
Clinton and Yeltsin also said they were committed to stepping up investment in Russia.

"President Clinton and President Yeltsin have committed to a joint initiative to stimulate investment and growth in Russia, deepen U.S.-Russian economic ties and accelerate Russia's integrations with global markets," they said in a statement.
This underscored the importance of Russia's transformation to a market economy, which was in the mutual interest of both countries, they said.
Yeltsin would implement a new legal regime that would demonstrate Russia's commitment to attracting foreign and domestic investment, the statement said.

"His highest economic priority is a tax regime that both meets the revenue needs of the Russian government and stimulates legitimate business, including actions on the value-added tax, excise tax, and both corporate and individual income taxes."
Because of changes in Russia's economy, the United States would extend Most Favored Nation status to Russia.

"Private banks, capital markets and commodity exchanges are emerging as the new institutions underpinning Russian economics. Inflation has been sharply reduced, and Russia has begun to enter international capital markets."

"United States and Russia will consider problems connected with the regulation of trade between the two countries, take steps to increase access to each other's markets, and establish the appropriate conditions to extend Most Favored Nation status to Russia on a permanent and unconditional basis."
